title: [YouPass Collect] - Class size of four states of Australia
prompt: The pie charts show the size of classes in primary schools in four states in Australia in 2010. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts provide information about the average number of primary school students per class in different Australian states in 2010.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, in all the examined areas, the majority of classes were comprised of fewer than 30 students each, with the class size of 21 to 25 students being the most common, except in South Australia. Meanwhile, the Australia Capital Territory had the smallest average class size compared to the other regions.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with smaller class sizes, Australia Capital Territory took the lead for classes with 20 students or fewer, at 38%, followed by South Australia, which was 3% lower. The corresponding percentages for New South Wales and Western Australia were smaller, both at 26%. In addition, classes of 21-25 students constituted more than half (51%) of the total in the Australia Capital Territory, which was nearly 10% higher than in Western Australia, where it stood at 42% in the same year. This category made up around one-third of all classes in the other two regions.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, the larger class size of 26 to 30 students was less prevalent, with the highest percentage observed in New South Wales at 33%, 5-6% higher than in both South Australia and Western Australia. The Australia Capital Territory only had 10% of its classes in this size bracket, and only 1% of their classes exceeded 30 students, while the figures for the remaining three states varied from 4% to 5%.
